items.title: FRC fines Saffery over its 2019 Greensill Capital audit
items.summary: The UK Financial Reporting Council sanctioned Saffery LLP and audit partner Michael Di Leto after they admitted 23 breaches of relevant requirements on the FY2019 audit of Greensill Capital (UK).
detail: The FRC notice is dated 16 November 2026. Saffery received a financial sanction of £581,250, cut from £750,000 by a 22.5% discount for admissions and early disposal. Di Leto was fined £124,000, reduced from £160,000. The FRC also declared that the 2019 audit report did not meet the requirements and ordered the firm to take steps to reduce the risk of repeat breaches.

According to City AM, the regulator described the breaches as serious and pervasive across the audit, while finding that they did not cause Greensill Capital's administration. The FRC opened its investigation in June 2021. Greensill's administrators had separately reached a £71 million settlement with Saffery.
items.why: A clear UK enforcement case on audit quality failures at a mid-tier firm, useful next to the ASIC Big Four complaints review in Australia.

items.title: S&P 500 posts its best week since April 2025 after a 5.6% rebound
items.summary: Wall Street ended the Thanksgiving week with its largest weekly gain in more than a year, led by AI stocks after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.
detail: In Friday's half-day session on 27 November the S&P 500 rose 1.60% to 7,297.49, the Nasdaq Composite gained about 2.3% to 24,129.50 and the Dow added 591.99 points to 50,774.94. For the week the S&P 500 gained about 5.6%, the Dow about 5.5% (its best week since October 2022) and the Nasdaq about 6.7%.

The rally followed a week in which the S&P 500 fell almost 9%. Nvidia rose 19.9% for the week after a 22.9% drop the week before. All three indexes are still down for November, and Monday 30 November is the last trading day of the month.
items.why: Shows how quickly AI-related sentiment is moving US equity valuations, with the Fed decision only days away.

items.title: Jobs data and the 8–9 December Fed meeting are the next tests for markets
items.summary: Reuters' week-ahead preview says investors will focus on the November US jobs report, with the Fed widely expected to raise rates by a quarter point at its December meeting.
detail: Economists polled by LSEG expect about 90,000 new jobs and an unemployment rate of 4.1% in the November payrolls report. The Fed is widely expected to lift rates by 25 basis points on 8–9 December to fight inflation.

The Cboe Volatility Index sat around 24, above its long-term median of 17.6. Since its 6 October record the S&P 500 was about 7% lower and the Nasdaq about 13% lower. Jensen Huang is due to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Thursday, and Salesforce and Marvell report results this week.
items.why: A Fed hike would push US yields and the dollar higher, which feeds directly into pressure on the rupiah and BI policy.

items.title: EU summit ends without a budget deal as own resources stay open
items.summary: European Council President António Costa said leaders did not reach agreement on the 2028–2034 EU budget at the special summit, and work on new own resources, including his proposed digital services levy, will continue.
detail: Costa told the press conference after the 26 November special European Council: "We didn't reach an agreement." On own resources he said "we will continue to work." His package includes five revenue streams that Euronews says would raise about €60 billion a year; the Commission's own estimate is €58.2 billion a year.

One element is a digital services tax meant to replace the contested CORE levy on large companies, expected to raise around €5 billion. A French source quoted by Euronews said the revenue side remains largely theoretical. France's Macron threatened to end budget talks if there is no deal in December.
items.why: An EU-level digital tax would sit alongside Pillar One and Pillar Two debates on how large multinationals are taxed.

items.title: Prabowo says about 60 people have been examined over stock manipulation
items.summary: Speaking at Bank Indonesia's annual meeting on 27 November, President Prabowo attacked share price manipulation and said around 60 people had been handed over for examination; OJK welcomed his backing on 28 November.
detail: Prabowo said wealthy actors were still "frying" stocks and that young people and small investors were the victims. He said, if he was not mistaken, about 60 people had been handed over to be examined.

OJK said it appreciated the president's support for firm enforcement, including the DSSA case, where Bareskrim has named suspects (reports differ on whether three or four). OJK fined PT Sinar Mas Tunggal Rp1.5 trillion over alleged manipulation between 2023 and 2026 and imposed administrative sanctions in 10 cases on 21 November. The crackdown comes as MSCI presses Indonesia over shareholding concentration and free float.
items.why: Market integrity enforcement is central to whether MSCI keeps Indonesia's status and foreign investors return to the IDX.

items.title: OECD gives Indonesia seven tax recommendations, including a lower PKP threshold
items.summary: The OECD Economic Surveys: Indonesia 2026 sets out seven recommendations to strengthen tax revenue, and analysts told Kontan the government should not adopt them all at once.
detail: Kontan reported on 27 November that the recommendations cover VAT on e-commerce and a plan to lower the VAT registration (PKP) threshold, among others. Analysts urged caution, warning against adopting every recommendation directly.

The report lands as DJP chases its 2026 target. Tax revenue to October was Rp1,796.8 trillion, or 76.2% of the APBN 2026 target, and DJP needed to collect around Rp500 trillion more in November and December.
items.why: Lowering the PKP threshold would pull many more small businesses into the VAT system, a live issue for Indonesian tax policy.

items.title: Tax Court transfer to the Supreme Court set for completion by 31 December
items.summary: The move of the Pengadilan Pajak's organisational, administrative and financial oversight from Kemenkeu to the Mahkamah Agung is to be finished by 31 December 2026, with full operation under the MA from January 2027.
detail: The shift follows Constitutional Court Decision No. 26/PUU-XXI/2023. Kemenkeu said the implementing Perpres had cleared harmonisation and was in administrative processing, with the aim of having it issued by the end of November. A 25 November report still described it as a target, and no signed Perpres has been confirmed.

Under the draft, Tax Court judges would become Supreme Court judges, while secretariat staff would remain Kemenkeu employees assigned to the MA for a set period. Through August 2026 the average administrative handling time for tax disputes was 11 days, against a 25-day benchmark in Law No. 14 of 2002.
items.why: Changes the institutional home of Indonesian tax dispute resolution, a core topic for tax dispute study.

items.title: Analysts see IHSG testing 5,500–5,600 on Monday
items.summary: After a 3.73% weekly gain, Phintraco Sekuritas expects the index to test 5,500–5,600 on 30 November if it holds above 5,350–5,450.
detail: IHSG closed Friday 27 November up 1.84% at 5,338. Technically the index is above its five-day moving average, with the negative histogram narrowing and Stochastic RSI turning at the pivot area.

Investors will watch the S&P Global manufacturing PMI, the trade balance and inflation data this week. Optimism that law enforcement against market manipulation will restore MSCI and foreign investor confidence is supporting the rebound, though foreign outflows this year have been large.
items.why: Ties market sentiment directly to regulatory enforcement and governance, an accounting and finance link worth tracking.

worth.title: Tax Court transfer to the Supreme Court set for completion by 31 December
worth.text: Indonesia's tax dispute system is about to change its institutional home. Worth following whether the Perpres is signed before the year-end deadline and how it treats judges and the secretariat.
